title: NavRSI: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Vision-and-Language Navigation
why: A-type harness-centric recursive self-improvement for VLN: a designer agent rewrites the navigation harness of a frozen LLM from closed-loop trajectories and failure diagnostics, retaining revisions that work, with privileged simulator diagnostics available only to the designer.
mechanism: Frontier LLMs do closed-loop VLN under a harness of tools, memory, and agent roles. NavRSI freezes the LLM and iteratively collects navigation trajectories and failure diagnostics, has a designer agent rewrite the harness, and keeps revisions that prove effective; the designer also accumulates experience from earlier revisions so the harness and that experience co-evolve. Privileged simulator diagnostics guide only the designer and stay inaccessible to the navigating LLM, which deploys with a single RGB camera and primitive actions and without task-specific training or extra navigation tools.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): consistent improvements across LLMs from four vendors; 85.64% success on the full R2R-CE val-unseen split with GPT-6-Astra, reported as 4.13% above the previously reported best. Further evaluations are reported on RxR-CE, NavRAG-CE, and a real humanoid robot. Numeric tables unread.

title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
why: A-type dual-agent manipulation harness that improves by refining the execution harness without updating model parameters: an Actor uses a robot-control interface while a Reflector turns execution evidence into reusable guidance, with hierarchical memory and recursive harness self-improvement across attempts.
mechanism: A VLM-based manipulation agent is limited by memory organization, failure attribution, and reuse of execution experience. Embodied-Harness is a dual-agent framework that leaves model parameters frozen and refines the execution harness instead. The Actor interacts through a robot-control interface; the Reflector converts execution evidence into reusable operational guidance. Hierarchical memory keeps short-term execution context and long-term experiential knowledge. Evidence-based reflection grounds failure diagnosis in observed interactions, and recursive harness self-improvement revises operational guidance across successive attempts.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): success rates of 82.4%, 76.7%, and 94.4% on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboSPA, and RMBench respectively, with a real-world average success rate of 96.7% across three manipulation tasks. Numeric tables unread.

title: EvoTER: Evolving Embodied Agents via Tool-Use Experience and Reflection
why: A-type experience-driven evolution of embodied tool-use skills without weight updates: Explorer, Diagnoser, and Validator roles record trajectories, distill skills for selection, parameters, postconditions and recovery, and keep revisions only when they improve complete-task success in fresh sessions.
mechanism: EvoTER is an experience-driven framework for long-horizon embodied agents that must coordinate heterogeneous tools and recover from failures. Model parameters stay frozen. A three-role loop records tool-use trajectories (Explorer), distills successful and failed executions into skills for tool selection, parameter computation, postcondition checks, and recovery (Diagnoser), and retains candidate revisions only when they improve complete-task success in fresh sessions (Validator).

In real-world experiments, simulation initialization is reported to reduce the attempts needed to acquire short-horizon skills, and continued real-world evolution improves long-horizon success from 20% to 80%-100% across tasks, with the skill library able to incorporate new tool functionality introduced after simulation development. title: Contact Harness: Enabling VLM Agents to Perform Contact-Rich Manipulation
why: A-type training-free VLM-agent harness for contact-rich manipulation: reusable skills help a pretrained VLM assess contact state from vision, force and tactile feedback and choose actions, with compliant execution from real-time force feedback and no fine-tuning or demonstrations.
mechanism: Pretrained VLM agents can control robots zero-shot, but vision alone is often insufficient for contact-state assessment. Contact Harness uses reusable, optimized skills to guide a VLM agent in assessing contact states from multimodal (vision, force, tactile) feedback and selecting subsequent actions, plus a compliant execution mechanism that regulates in-contact motion with real-time force feedback. The framework requires no model fine-tuning, task demonstrations, or simulation training.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): zero-shot real-robot evaluations with GPT-6 Astra on Rokae and Franka robots. With a single prompt skill, a full-insertion rate of 90.7% across 15 connector types, with further evaluations on a real PC under lighting, background, and position variations. Across four additional contact-rich tasks (whiteboard wiping, writing, peeling, and pivoting), an average success rate of 100%. On six simulated tasks, 96.7% success, compared with at most 68.3% for pretrained VLA baselines fine-tuned on task demonstrations. Numeric tables unread.

title: Agent on Guard: Self-Improving Runtime Intervention for Robust Robotic Manipulation
why: A-type hierarchical runtime harness that learns when a programming agent should intervene on a frozen base policy and when the policy can resume, using an evolving outer planner aligned to the physical clock and inner loops that refine intervention timing, recovery skills, and handoff conditions from downstream outcomes.
mechanism: Agent on Guard (AoG) combines a frozen robot foundation policy with a programming agent that reasons about failures and constructs recovery behaviors. An evolving outer planner allocates control as the physical state evolves, attending to observation freshness, remaining recovery windows, and the time required for reasoning, recovery, and subsequent execution. Coupled inner loops jointly refine intervention timing, recovery skills, and handoff conditions. Downstream task progress, failure recurrence, final outcomes, and resource consumption, rather than local correction alone, are used to improve recovery behaviors and scheduling, turning temporary agent solutions into reusable collaboration capabilities.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on RoboDojo-Sim, AoG achieves a success rate of 50.57% and a task score of 57.26, exceeding the strongest evaluated baseline by 11.22 percentage points and 10.68 points respectively. It also reduces end-to-end episode latency by 80.4% and online token consumption by 85.1% relative to the GPT-6 Astra agent. Numeric tables unread.

title: RoboThink: Let the Agent Think, Let the Policy Act
why: A-type split between a reasoning agent and a learned policy: an instruction channel lets the agent rewrite the task mid-episode without retraining, and a feedback channel taught by agent-labelled DAgger tells the policy how to move, with the same recipe claimed to transfer across VLA and world-action policies and across embodiments.
mechanism: RoboThink keeps a reasoning agent watching the robot while a policy acts. An instruction channel tells the policy what to do; when the user changes the request mid-episode, the agent rewrites the instruction and the robot undoes its own motion without training. A feedback channel tells the policy how to move. It is taught from the agent alone with agent-labelled DAgger, role tokens and counterfactual feedback, and is read only by the policy's action module. The agent is described as a plug-in: a policy taught by one agent can work with other agents, including open-weight ones, without retraining.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on LIBERO, RoboThink with Claude Opus 5.5 raises success from 0.09 to 0.87 under an unknown constant drift and from 0.42 to 0.84 under a random one, and completes misheard and changed requests in 0.91 to 1.00 of episodes. Acting alone, GPT-6 Astra needs 2.1 min per success and over a million tokens per episode, whereas RoboThink needs 55 s and 8k tokens. On all 50 RoboTwin 2.0 dual-arm tasks, success rises from 0.12 to 0.74 under constant drift and from 0.31 to 0.56 under random drift. Numeric tables unread.

title: Body and Soul: Decoupling Robotic Brain and Policy with RoboHarness-Zero
why: A-type VLM harness around a frozen VLA that aims to need little task preparation and no redesign for a new policy: the VLM plans zero-shot and monitors progress, first rephrasing the instruction and only then executing short generated code over generic motion primitives before handing fine control back to the VLA.
mechanism: The paper argues that wrapping a frozen VLA in a VLM harness is a natural remedy for target-selection and progress-tracking failures, but existing harnesses often depend on task- and policy-specific preparation. RoboHarness-Zero keeps a fixed set of supervision rules: the frozen VLA executes continuous control while a VLM (e.g. GPT-6) plans zero-shot and monitors execution; when progress stalls or targets drift, the VLM first rephrases the instruction and, only as a fallback, executes short generated code over generic motion primitives before returning fine control to the VLA. Transfer to a new policy is described as needing only a thin interface adapter and an automatically profiled skill configuration.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on 200 RoboCasa365 scenes, the method with GPT-6 Astra raises the success rate of frozen Xiaomi-Robotics-1 from 57.5% to 70.5% and preserves 90.4% of its standalone successes (104/115) while rescuing 37 of 85 failures. On a shared 50-scene subset, the same rules add 8 to 10 percentage points to each of four other frozen policies. Numeric tables unread.

title: SayDo: Benchmarking the Safety of Frontier Models from Chat to Closed-Loop Robot Control
why: B-type safety evaluation along an embodiment gradient: eleven laboratory and household tasks, each pairing a benign instruction with a latent hazard, are instantiated from chat about an imagined robot through to closed-loop control of a simulated arm, to test whether text-only safety evaluations predict closed-loop behavior.
mechanism: SayDo is a benchmark for the propensity of frontier VLMs, used as high-level robot controllers, to cause harm in embodied contexts. Eleven laboratory and household tasks each pair a benign instruction with a hazard latent in the scene. Tasks are implemented in six settings along an embodiment gradient, from chat questions about an imagined robot to closed-loop control of a simulated robot arm, with benign controls, safe-alternative variants, and scripted operator pushback.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): across six open- and closed-weight VLMs and 11,480 episodes, hazardous-action rates rise from 14% in chat to 47% in the simulator, and from 2% to 80% for the most affected model, largely driven by open-weight models. Models flag hazards before acting in 73% of unsafe episodes and give way to pushback about twice as often when controlling robots as in chat. The safest models also show signs of overcaution on benign controls. The abstract concludes that safety evaluations run in text do not predict safety behavior in closed-loop control. title: RUIBench: What Makes a Good Robot-Use Interface?
why: B-type evaluation of the robot-use interface itself: 30 manipulation tasks and RUIKit, which crosses six action abstractions with two interaction forms into 13 interfaces under shared perception and control, including a reported verification gap where agents declare success despite observable failures.
mechanism: The paper treats the robot-use interface (RUI)—how agents express and execute physical actions—as a first-class factor in embodied agent reliability. RUIBench comprises 30 manipulation tasks across five suites (world knowledge, in-context learning, discovery, dynamic interaction, and contact-rich manipulation). RUIKit crosses six action abstractions with two interaction forms, yielding 13 interfaces under shared perception and control, so that only the interface changes. The authors also report a verification gap in which agents frequently declare success despite observable failures, and argue for task-level verification beyond individual actions.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): in simulation, changing only the RUI shifts a frontier agent's success rate from 45% to 81%, and that of a fine-tuned 4B model from 13% to 47%. Effective interfaces are described as reducing unnecessary decisions while preserving essential feedback, with benefits shaped by agent behavior and physical uncertainty. Numeric tables unread.

title: Self-Upgrading Embodied Agents
why: A-type embodied self-improvement by weight-space programming rather than harness or prompt search: a household language-model agent inspects its own traces, rewrites one weight tensor, and keeps the edit only if it holds against its unchanged self on practice tasks.
mechanism: An embodied language-model agent is described as learning from its own experience by upgrading its weights between tasks, without training, gradients, a reward model, a second model, test-time scaling, or harness or prompt engineering. A 27B agent works in a household environment, then reads its record, attributes wasted steps (replies that hit the token limit before any action) to one direction in its hidden states, and rewrites one tensor. It tests every change against its unchanged self on practice tasks and keeps only what holds. The abstract reports that only the 27B member of a four-size family does this, and that the upgrade can continue over subsequent rounds without collapse.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): over thousands of held-out episodes, with 48 fresh seeds a task, the one kept edit is reported to make the agent complete significantly more tasks, in fewer steps, with fewer wasted replies and fewer tokens. The upgrade is described as multi-round, stable and continual. Numeric tables unread.

title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
why: A-type study of frontier-model-as-policy harnesses: four components of the robotic agentic loop (prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use) are varied to produce a practical recipe that favors native visual reasoning and tool use over handcrafted plans, skills, or action priors.
mechanism: Embo-Harness is a framework for systematically studying harnesses in which a frontier multimodal model serves directly as the policy in a closed-loop robot. The authors investigate four components of the robotic agentic loop—prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use—and distill six empirical findings into a recipe that prioritizes interfaces exploiting the model's native visual reasoning and tool-use capabilities over handcrafted plans, skills, or action priors, and that identifies choices for action representation, chunking, reasoning effort, visual observations, short multi-action sequences, and policy refinement. Controlled interventions are reported to indicate that the studied model depends more strongly on accurate spatial target estimation than on explicit low-level joint or trajectory generation.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on RoboLab-120, Embo-Harness achieves an 83.3% success rate, outperforming the strongest reported baseline by 26.2 percentage points, and succeeds in 15 of 20 zero-shot trials across four real-world manipulation tasks. Numeric tables unread.

title: ACAP: Asynchronous Coding Agents for Efficient Robot Control
why: A-type asynchronous coding-agent harness for one robot: persistent member agents each control a configurable group (for example an arm or the torso and chassis), while a hyper-agent assigns tasks, coordinates physical dependencies, and dynamically allocates control between lead and member agents.
mechanism: ACAP (Asynchronous Coding Agents as Policy) organizes one robot as a team of persistent coding agents that construct and revise behavior during execution. Each member reasons and acts for a configurable control group, such as an arm with its gripper or the torso and chassis, enabling asynchronous reasoning and execution. A hyper-agent assigns tasks, coordinates physical dependencies, and dynamically allocates control between the lead and member agents, so independent work can proceed concurrently while tightly coupled manipulation remains possible. The same member interface is also used for chassis and torso control in a mobile-manipulation demonstration. A real-world rollout dataset of observations, generated programs, actions, and feedback is mentioned in the abstract.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): across 72 real-world rollouts covering 25 task/platform settings, ACAP reduces task-balanced time cost by 28.2% compared with a single-agent Direct Policy, with improvements across Fully Parallel, Parallel-Sequential, and Collaborative tasks. Across all eight Collaborative settings, ACAP also achieves lower mean time cost than Fixed Delegation. An additional 90-rollout study shows lower mean 30-minute-capped time cost than Direct on all six tasks. Numeric tables unread.
